pr.title: Use `PtrMetadata` instead of `Len` in slice drop shims
pr.description:
I tried to do a bigger change in #134297 which didn't work, so here's the part I really wanted: Removing another use of `Len`, in favour of `PtrMetadata`.

Split into two commits where the first just adds a test, so you can look at the second commit to see how the drop shim for an array changes with this PR.

Reusing the same reviewer from the last one:
r? BoxyUwU
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR is a semantics-preserving MIR-lowering refactor in AddMovesForPackedDrops, not a runtime-bug fix. The old lowering computed the loop bound with `Len((*_1))` (or `Len(array_place)` for arrays); the new lowering unsizes the array pointer to `*mut [T]` and uses `PtrMetadata(copy ptr)`, or directly uses `PtrMetadata(copy _1)` for slices. Both read the same slice/array length, and the unsizing cast preserves the array length. The drop loops, cleanup loops, and element drops are otherwise unchanged. Therefore there is no source-grounded pair of ordinary Rust functions whose original and transformed executions produce different values on defined inputs under Miri; forcing a difference would require an unrelated rewrite or invalid MIR (such as applying PtrMetadata to the dereferenced place), which the PR does not do. This patch is suitable for differential MIR expectations, not a runtime differential counterexample.

analysis.summary: AddMovesForPackedDrops lowers slice/array drop shims by deriving the loop bound from the fat-pointer metadata via PtrMetadata instead of Rvalue::Len. Array drop shims now take a raw pointer to the array, unsize it to a slice pointer, elaborate the drop loop over (*slice_ptr), and read the length from that slice pointer with PtrMetadata.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, both slice and array drop loops used the same helper: `fn drop_loop_pair(&mut self, ety: Ty<'tcx>)` computed the loop bound with `self.assign(len.into(), Rvalue::Len(self.place))` and dispatched `ty::Slice(ety) => self.drop_loop_pair(*ety)`. For arrays without a statically unrolled body, `open_drop_for_array` also ended in `self.drop_loop_pair(ety)`, so the length came from `Len` on the array/slice place itself.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation replaced here derives the drop-loop bound with `Rvalue::Len(self.place)` on the dereferenced array/slice place (for slices, the test shows `_2 = Len((*_1));`). The optimized transformation instead renames the helper to `drop_loop_pair_for_slice`, requires `self.place.projection` to be exactly `[PlaceElem::Deref]`, and emits `Rvalue::UnaryOp(UnOp::PtrMetadata, Operand::Copy(Place::from(self.place.local)))`. For arrays it first emits `array_ptr = &raw mut <array place>`, then `slice_ptr = move array_ptr as *mut [T] (PointerCoercion(Unsize, Implicit))`, temporarily replaces `self.place` with `(*slice_ptr)`, elaborates the slice loop, restores the original array place, and inserts a delegate block that jumps to the slice loop. This PR describes the change as removing another use of `Len`, so the old Len-based lowering is the baseline for differential MIR checks rather than a claimed runtime bug.
analysis.inputDomain: `std::ptr::drop_in_place` shims for slice and array types whose element type needs drop, specifically `[String]` and `[String; 42]` in the regression test; more generally `ty::Slice(ety)` and `ty::Array(ety, size)` lowered through the non-unrolled drop-loop path during AddMovesForPackedDrops.
analysis.trigger: Elaborating a drop shim for an array that does not take the unrolled drop path, or for a slice, so the generated code must compute the number of elements at runtime for both the normal drop loop and its cleanup/unwind loop.
preconditions: The place passed to `drop_loop_pair_for_slice` has projection exactly `[PlaceElem::Deref]`; otherwise the code reaches `span_bug!("Expected place for slice drop shim to be *_n, but it's {:?}")`.
For arrays, a raw mutable pointer to the whole array is created and then unsized to `*mut [T]` before metadata is read.
The slice element type `ety` is known and used to build `Ty::new_slice(tcx, ety)` and the `*mut [T]` pointer type.
Both the normal and cleanup drop loops must use the same computed length and retain the unwind/cleanup structure.
pitfalls: PtrMetadata must be applied to the pointer local, e.g. `PtrMetadata(copy _1)` or `PtrMetadata(copy _3)`, not to the dereferenced place such as `(*_1)`; the test diff explicitly changes `Len((*_1))` to `PtrMetadata(copy _1)`.

For arrays the pointer must first be unsized from `*mut [T; N]` to `*mut [T]`; reading metadata from the thin array pointer does not represent the array length. The recorded MIR shows `_2 = &raw mut (*_1); _3 = move _2 as *mut [std::string::String] (PointerCoercion(Unsize, Implicit)); _4 = PtrMetadata(copy _3);`.
The elaborator temporarily replaces `self.place` with `(*slice_ptr)` and must restore the saved array place afterward, or subsequent drop elaboration would use the wrong place.
The new projection assertion deliberately rejects arbitrary places; do not generalize the helper to field or index projections without adjusting the metadata source.
Do not conflate this length-derivation rewrite with borrowing restrictions or post-copy overwrites; neither condition is what this patch changes.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the mir-opt regression test `tests/mir-opt/slice_drop_shim.rs` with `// EMIT_MIR core.ptr-drop_in_place.[String].AddMovesForPackedDrops.before.mir` and the added `// EMIT_MIR core.ptr-drop_in_place.[String;42].AddMovesForPackedDrops.before.mir`, instantiated by `std::ptr::drop_in_place::<[String]>` and `std::ptr::drop_in_place::<[String; 42]>`. Compare the decoded MIR: the slice shim must use `_2 = PtrMetadata(copy _1);` rather than `_2 = Len((*_1));`, and the array shim must contain the raw-pointer creation, `PointerCoercion(Unsize, Implicit)` cast to `*mut [String]`, `PtrMetadata(copy _3)`, and both normal and cleanup loops counting to that length. Construct two compiler variants differing only in how the loop bound is derived (Len on the place versus PtrMetadata on the slice pointer) and verify the expected MIR difference without claiming execution.
